description_raw: The project will implement the third section of the Sibiu – Pitești Motorway (A1) between the localities of Cornetu and Tigveni (Vâlcea and Argeș counties), which will have a length of 37.4 km and will include 52 bridges, one ecoduct, one tunnel, two interchanges, two service areas, and a maintenance and coordination center. The main beneficiaries of this project are: users of the transport network (drivers and transport operators), as well as local communities. The segment targeted by this contract is part of the strategically important Sibiu-Pitești Highway project, part of the TEN-T Core network, which will complete the Rhine-Danube corridor, providing a fast and safe connection between the western border with Hungary and the port of Constanța. The completion of the entire highway will reduce travel time, improve road safety, and modernize the transport infrastructure. Currently, traffic between Sibiu and Pitești takes place on DN7, a crowded and dangerous route that causes frequent delays and has a low average speed (60 km/h). Between 2012 and 2018, road accidents on DN7 increased by 40%, making this road dangerous and inefficient for both passenger and freight transport. To address these issues, the Sibiu-Pitești highway will provide a fast and safe route, uninterrupted, between Sibiu and Pitești, crossing the counties of Sibiu, Vâlcea, and Argeș. The route will include cities and localities such as: Șelimbăr, Tălmaciu, Turnu Roșu; Câineni, Racovița, Perișani; Sălătrucu, Șuici, Cepari, Tigveni, Curtea de Argeș, Băiculești, Merișani, Budeasa, and Bascov. The project is divided into five sections:• Sibiu-Boița (13.17 km)• Boița-Cornetu (31.33 km)• Cornetu-Tigveni (37.40 km)• Tigveni-Curtea de Argeș (9.86 km)• Curtea de Argeș-Pitești (30.35 km) Main benefits include:• Reduced travel time and increased safety: Provides modern infrastructure for passengers and transporters.• Strategic connections: Creates a continuous corridor between Western Europe and the Black Sea, facilitating international trade.• Economic development: Stimulates investments, creates jobs, and supports local businesses and tourism.• Pollution and congestion reduction: Eases heavy traffic on DN7, bringing direct environmental and health benefits for communities. The construction of the highway will modernize Romania’s transport network, reducing congestion, travel time, and the risk of accidents. This project will have a major impact on the national economy, facilitating freight transport and improving the country’s connection to the European network.More info at: https://fonduri.mt.ro/programul-transport-pt-2021-2027/proiectele-pt/autostrada-sibiu-pitesti-sectiunea-3-cornetu-tigveni  You can also find more information on the beneficiary’s dedicated project page: https://www.cnadnr.ro/ro/proiecte/autostrada-sibiu-pite%C8%99ti-sec%C8%9Biunea-3

originalDescription: The general objective of the Sibiu-Pitesti motorway, as defined in the MPGT, is to improve the economic efficiency of Romanian transport, by improving the travel time between Sibiu and Pitesti and implicitly improving connectivity at regional level. The objective of the corridor is to provide direct access to the Black Sea through a unified motorway profile as well as to other countries through border connections. The new motorway is the first to cross the Carpathian Mountains and will bring significant development opportunities for all communities from the north to the south of Romania. Thus, the project aims to provide an appropriate mix of ‘high-quality road’ infrastructure, as part of the national infrastructure network, to accommodate long-distance freight and passenger traffic, as well as local traffic specific to the metropolitan area, while ensuring an adequate level of traffic safety and security.

description_raw: Enhancing mobility and connectivity through the development and modernisation of Bucharest's ring road infrastructure.The "Integrated Infrastructure for the Orbital Area of Bucharest" project addresses the need for improved mobility and connectivity in the Bucharest metropolitan area. Bucharest, the capital city of Romania, faces significant traffic congestion and accessibility challenges due to its expanding population and economic activities. The project focuses on developing and modernising essential road infrastructure, with an emphasis on enhancing mobility on the central Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) road network. The objective is to facilitate better interconnectivity between national roads, motorways, and Bucharest's local road network, ultimately improving traffic safety and access to the city.Objectives:Construct the Southern Sector of the Bucharest Bypass Motorway, including new motorway sections and supporting infrastructure.Modernise existing sections of the Bucharest Ring Road for enhanced capacity and safety.Improve traffic flow and intersection functionality at key junctions such as Domnești, Oltenița, Berceni, and Mogoșoaia.Increase accessibility to the TEN-T network from local roads and Bucharest.Enhance traffic safety conditions.Key Features and Activities:Construction of 51.195 km of new motorway for the Bucharest Bypass Motorway.Modernisation of 20.274 km of the existing Bucharest Ring Road, incorporating new bridges, overpasses, and parking areas.Development of advanced intersection structures including level roundabouts and collecting roads.Widening of specific road sections for improved traffic capacity.Establishment of maintenance centres and service areas to support traffic operations.Target Audience:Citizens of Bucharest and neighbouring regionsLocal and national commutersTransport and logistics companiesPublic authorities overseeing infrastructure managementImpact:Improved traffic flow and reduced congestion within Bucharest and its orbital area.Enhanced economic activity through better accessibility and connectivity.Increased safety and reduced travel times, fostering social and economic benefits.Strengthened territorial cohesion between Bucharest and surrounding regions.

originalDescription: The overall objective of the development of and integrated road infrastructure in Bucharest orbital area (hereby called “the project”) is to provide the package of integrated measures aimed to meet the requirements of Regulation EU no. 1315/2013 on the TEN-T Core network. Thus, the project aims to provide an appropriate mixture of “high quality road” infrastructure, as part of the national infrastructure network, to accommodate long distance freight and passenger traffic as well as local traffic specific to the metropolitan area, while ensuring an appropriate level of traffic safety and security. After the project is Finalised, it will contribute to the Accomplishment of the general objective of LIOP, 2014-2020, Priority Axis no. 1 Improving mobility by developing the TEN-T and subway network, Specific Objective 1.1: “Increasing mobility on the central TEN-T road network”. The specific objectives of the project are: • Component 1 – Bucharest Bypass Motorway – Southern Sector: construction of 51.195 km of 2x2 new motorway section, including 9 bridges, 33 overpasses, 5 interchanges, 4 parking areas, 1 Coordination and Maintenance Center, 1 Maintenance Supporting Point and 1 service area; • Component 2 – Modernisation of Bucharest Ring Road between A1 – DN7 and DN2 – A2 – Modernisation of 20.274 km of national road on A1 – DN7 and DN2 – A2 Sectors, part of the existing Bucharest Bypass (of which 8.750 km for A1 – DN7 Sector and 11.524 km for DN2 – A2 Sector), including 16 intersections, the construction of 3 bridges, 4 overpasses and 2 parking areas, the rehabilitation of 1 bridge and 3 overpasses; • Component 3 – Domnesti DJ602 Intersection, including 2 level Roundabouts, 2 collecting roads; • Component 4 – Oltenita DN4 and Berceni DJ401 Intersections and widening the Ring Road in between, including 4 levelabouts, and 4 collecting roads, as well as the widening of DNCB section between them (6.1 km); • Component 5 – Mogosoaia DN1A Intersection • Component 6 – Modernisation of Bucharest Ring Road between A1 – DN5- Widening to 4 lanes of 14.525 km ring road, including 5 intersections with classified roads, the construction of 3 new passages, 3 parking areas and the rehabilitation of 1 passage; Additionally, the project implementation will: • Ensure an adequate interconnectivity of all inter-regional corridors, with the network of adjacent national roads and motorways; • Ensure adequate accessibility to the TEN-T network from/to the local road network and the city of Bucharest. • Ensure a higher quality of the existing infrastructure by providing improved traffic safety conditions.
